liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer describes this version as really powerful and a peak of the show; The space segment is included within the Other One track [1][27]
- **MIssissippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (1 review): Reviewer hears a fairly mellow opener to the night [18]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Reviewer finds this version best in its surging mid-section jams, around 6:15 to 7:30 [18]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Reviewer finds it pleasant but too contentedly nice, lacking sensuality [18]
- **Queen Jane Approximately** (1 review): Reviewer believes this was the first one played without Dylan and ranks it in their top five [19]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Reviewer calls it well paced but fruitless, and thinks it does not belong in a second set [23]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Reviewer counts Fire coming out of Hell In A Bucket among the night's highest moments [27]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd87-09-08 t01 Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd87-09-08 t02 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd87-09-08 t03 They Love Each Other**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd87-09-08 t04 Queen Jane Approximately**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd87-09-08 t05 Row Jimmy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd87-09-08 t06 The Music Never Stopped**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd87-09-08 t07 Don't Ease Me In**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd87-09-08 t08 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-09-08.141882.ultramatrix.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 19 songs; 139 min [1]
- **gd87-09-08.sbd.miller.20994.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 140 min; rated 3.36/5 by 11 [3]. Said about its sound: Soundboard recording is reported to sound very good and was still available to download [20]
- **gd1987-09-08.sbd.unknown.7468.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 136 min [4]. Said about its sound: This soundboard copy has a cut at 2:12 with about five seconds missing, and fades out during the final verse [4]
- **gd1987-09-08.nak300.andrewf.74162.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 17 songs; 137 min [5]
- **gd1987-09-08.176263.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 17 songs; 136 min [6]
- **gd1987-09-08.nakcm304.suraci.82309.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 17 songs; 135 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [11]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds good for its type [21]

## Around the show

- Police around the Providence Civic Center arrested fans for minor offenses like drinking beer in paid parking lots; over 100 jailed nightly [16]
- Inside, the venue felt small and intimate, holding roughly 16,000 people, and the reviewer saw it as the last run there [16]
- Reviewer recalls heat and a Shakedown Street scene in the parking lot; a tall caped man held a pole of street signs [24]
- Reviewer sees it as an overlooked show from the In the Dark era with a good setlist [21]
- Reviewer calls it solid, tight and zippy like much of that year, though nothing earth shattering [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-09-08.141882.ultramatrix.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Ultramatrix PCM > PCM [1]
- **gd87-09-08.sbd.miller.20994.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD -> PCM -> Dat -> CD -> EAC -> SHN Converted To SHN by Charlie Miller [3]
- **gd1987-09-08.sbd.unknown.7468.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Andrew Pitner; source: Unknown Soundboard [4]
- **gd1987-09-08.nak300.andrewf.74162.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Andrew F; transferred by Andrew F; source: AUD, Nakamichi CM-300's with CP-4 shotgun capsules > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90 cassettes, with no Dolby [5]. Also: Nakamichi 300 source; the tape flip in Space was patched with audience-source audio from the LMA, using Soundforge [5]
- **gd1987-09-08.176263.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Doug Lamarre; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Doug Lamarre's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [6]. Also: A 0:49 patch in the Drums > Space transition combines Nakamichi 300 and Sennheiser ME-80 sources from other tapers [6]
- **gd1987-09-08.nakcm304.suraci.82309.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Tony Suraci; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: Nak CM304's>Sony D5M [11]
